findings.claim: Every new attribute is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists on .NET Framework 4.0+ and netstandard2.0, and has AttributeTargets.Class there. So a consumer project targeting net4x or netstandard2.0 gets generated formatters and resolvers with no attribute. That breaks the criterion 'All generated code is decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage'. The derived criterion only permits conditional emission where the attribute does not exist. The same guard appears in EnumTemplate.tt, StringKeyFormatterTemplate.tt, UnionTemplate.tt, ResolverTemplate.tt and CompositeResolverTemplate.tt, and in their .cs counterparts.

receipt_plan.detail: Run tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/Receipts/ExcludeFromCodeCoverageLegacyTargetsTests.cs, GeneratedTypesAreExcludedWhenTargetingFrameworksThatHaveTheAttribute("NETFRAMEWORK") and ("NETSTANDARD2_0"). Each parses the input with that preprocessor symbol defined, against references that contain the attribute. It asserts that every generated type, or a type containing it, carries ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute. It fails on head because the #if strips the attribute.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Always-on with no setting. Every template (formatter, string-key formatter, enum, union, resolver, composite resolver and the helper/cache nested classes) unconditionally writes [global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] before the generated type. Nothing in GeneratorOptions or the attributes changes.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: On by default with an opt-out. Add a boolean option, e.g. a GeneratorOptions/FormattersOptions property read from an analyzer config key, or a property on GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute, defaulting to true. Each template emits the attribute line only when that option is true, so users who want generated code counted in coverage can turn it off.
